dialogue_text: I am Time.
speaker: SAMAY

dialogue_text: I cannot forget Indraprastha, Mamashree... It burns behind my eyes, even in sleep.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Burns... because it is greater than Hastinapura?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Because they built it out of nothing — and the whole world sings their praises for it! Yudhishthira is called the righteous one. Arjuna — the greatest archer alive. Bhima, a hero without equal. Even their younger brothers stand as kings beside them, as equals... while I stand in my own father's shadow.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Then do not fight them where they stand strongest, pyaare bhanje...
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Then tell me where, Mamashree. Where is their weakness?
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: You cannot defeat Yudhishthira with swords. His true strength is his Dharma. So we shall not fight his strength — we shall turn it into his prison.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: I do not want merely to defeat them, Mamashree. I want to see their pride broken... crawling... before my own eyes.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Then let the dice do, bhanje, what your armies never could...
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Welcome, dear Yudhishthira. It is a rare honour to have the King of Dharma himself at my dice board...
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, I have accepted your invitation in good faith. Let the game begin.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: Mamashree... the board is ready.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Indeed, pyare bhanje... Today, fortune shall decide everything.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Pyaare bhanje Duryadhana... what do you put at stake?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, I put my entire wealth at stake.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: How about you, Dharamraj Yudhisthir... what do you put at stake?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, I will play as an equal; I also pledge my wealth.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: ha ha... I win.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Your wealth is gone, Yudhishthira.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Pyaare bhanje Duryadhana... next, what do you put at stake?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, as the regent, I would like to put Hastinapura at stake.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: How about you, Dharamraj Yudhisthir... what do you put at stake?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, a kingdom for a kingdom; I also pledge Indraprastha.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: ha ha... I win.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharamraj... Yudhishthira, your Indraprastha is no longer yours now.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Bhratashree, stop this game! Can you not see where this road leads?
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: I have given my word. A Kshatriya does not break it — not even to save himself.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: A word that destroys everything we have built is not worth keeping!
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: Bhratashree... if this continues, there will be nothing left to call our own.
speaker: ARJUNA

dialogue_text: A king does not turn away from a challenge once he has accepted it. This is my burden to carry, not yours.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: And when the challenge itself becomes the weapon that destroys you, Bhratashree?
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj, wealth gone, kingdom gone... here is your chance to reclaim it; what do you put at stake to gain both back?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, I have my anuj, my dearest Nakul, who will help me reclaim my kingdom and wealth.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: Nakula.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Bhratashree... Even me?
speaker: NAKULA

dialogue_text: I have followed you through every fortune, because you are our elder. I will not turn against you now — but my heart tells me this is wrong.
speaker: NAKULA

dialogue_text: ha ha... my loyal dices never fail me!
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj... Nakula is no longer yours; he is now our slave.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj... what would you do now to reclaim your losses?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, I have my anuj, my dearest Sahadeva, who will not hestitate to put himself to gain back our losses.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: We are yours to stake, Bhratashree. But tell me — was this wisdom, or was it pride?
speaker: SAHADEVA

dialogue_text: ha ha... here again, my dices do it for me!
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharamraj... Sahadeva is no longer yours; he is also our slave.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj... what is next that you have to pledge?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, my dearest anuj Arjuna will win us back all that we lost.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: These hands have never once missed their mark, Bhratashree. Yet they cannot rise against my own elder brother.
speaker: ARJUNA

dialogue_text: ha ha... look how my dices are even powerful than the mightly Gandhiva that Arjuna holds with pride!
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj... Arjuna is no longer yours; he is also our slave.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj, you are running out of options... what do you have next to pledge?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Mamashree, my dearest anuj Bheema surely will restore our pride... our everything.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: I obey you because you are my elder, Bhratashree. Do not ask me to obey what I know, in my very bones, to be wrong.
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: ha ha... my dices today have acquired divine power!
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj... Bhima is no longer yours; he is also our slave.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: What remains, Yudhishthira?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: ...Myself.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: No! Bhratashree... no — not this!
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: You have lost yourself, O dharmaraj Yudhishthira. There is nothing left of the righteous king now.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: There is still one thing left upon this board.
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Draupadi.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj... the one who never takes a wrong step, would you pledge your beloved Draupadi?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Bhratashree, you are the wisest amongst us all... please do not take this grave mis-step.
speaker: ARJUNA

dialogue_text: Arjuna, what I am about to do is the best for all of us brothers... our praja.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: Mamamshree... yes, I pledge Draupadi.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: ha ha!
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dharmaraj... is it a surpise that you now lost your most precious gift — your Panchali?
speaker: SHAKUNI

dialogue_text: Dushasana!
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Yes, bhratashree.
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: Bring Draupadi to the Sabha. Let her hear, with her own ears, what her husbands have done.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Dushasana? Why have you come to me at this hour?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: You have been summoned to the Sabha.
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: By whom?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: By Duryodhana.
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: For what reason?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: You have been won.
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: Won?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: In the game of dice.
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: Go back, Dushasana. Ask Yudhishthira one question for me — only one.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: What question?
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: Did he lose himself before he staked me... or after?If he had already lost himself... what right — tell me, what right did he have left to stake me?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Bhratashree, Draupadi has refused to come, and instead is asking a question.
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: Dushasana! A slave has no right to ask any question; drag her into this sabha immediately!
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Panchali! You are no longer a Maharani; you are a daasi, and your place rests on my lap; come here.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Careful, Duryadhana; watch what you speak, for you will pay for each such word that you utter...
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: I have been dragged here against my will, before the eyes of this entire Sabha, and insulted by Duryadhana.I ask the elders gathered here...Am I won?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: I ask again, and I will keep asking until someone answers me.Did Yudhishthira lose himself... before he staked me?Or did he stake me first?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Pitamaha... you are the eldest in this Sabha. You have lived through more Dharma than any of us ever will. So tell me: If a man has already lost himself... does he still have the right to stake another human being?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Putri... Dharma, in this moment, is very difficult to understand.
speaker: BHISHMA

dialogue_text: Then what use is a Dharma so difficult, so tangled, that it cannot even protect a woman standing right before your eyes, begging to be seen?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Draupadi speaks the truth. This should never ever have been allowed to happen.
speaker: VIDURA

dialogue_text: The game has been played. The result stands clear before all of you.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: No, Duryodhana. A wrong does not become right simply because the dice have fallen in your favour.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Enough of this argument! She was staked. She was lost. The result must be accepted.
speaker: KARNA

dialogue_text: Karna... you call yourself a great warrior. Then answer me plainly: is a woman a thing, an object, to be won or lost at a game of dice?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: I know... I know this Sabha has stepped onto dangerous ground...
speaker: BHISHMA

dialogue_text: Then say it aloud, Pitamaha! Say the words that this MUST stop, now, before it goes further!
speaker: VIDURA

dialogue_text: You all know, in your hearts, that this is wrong. Yet every one of you waits for someone else to speak first. Tell me — has silence itself become your Dharma?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: I looked at you, O mighhty Gadadhari Bhima. I looked at you, Arjuna, the most powerful dhanurdhar wielding the Gandiva. I looked at every one of you, one by one... And I waited.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: I waited for just one of you to rise... and say...Enough.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Draupadi... please...
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: I know you are angry, Bhima. I can see the fire in your eyes from here. Then why — tell me why — are your hands still?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Because Bharatashree Yudhishthira is our elder brother, and I am bound to him!
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: And because he is your elder, must you obey him even when every fibre of your being screams that something is monstrously wrong?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: I no longer know what is worse — to disobey my brother... or to stand here, and simply watch this happen to you.
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: We are bound by his word, Panchali. It is not so simple as raising a bow.
speaker: ARJUNA

dialogue_text: Bound by his word... or bound by the fear of what it means to break it?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: My hands can defeat armies, Panchali. But they cannot rise against my elder brother — not even for you.
speaker: ARJUNA

dialogue_text: We followed him into prosperity, Draupadi. We will follow him into hardship too.
speaker: NAKULA

dialogue_text: But today... today, following him is breaking our hearts, one by one.
speaker: SAHADEVA

dialogue_text: Then tell me, Yudhishthira, since you are the one who staked me. What is Dharma now?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Draupadi... I have no answer that can undo what has already been done.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: You call this... Dharma?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: I believed, with my whole heart, that keeping my word was Dharma.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: And now? What do you believe now?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Now... I see that my belief has brought nothing but suffering upon everyone I love.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: I am not asking any of you to abandon Dharma. I am asking you — what is Dharma, when the very rules meant to protect us are twisted into a weapon against us?
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Enough talk. Dushasana! Take off her royal garments — let this Sabha see her as a slave should be seen.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Duryodhana! Do not touch her — I warn you!
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: You have lost every right to command anything in this hall, Bhima.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: You may have won a game, Duryodhana. Do not, for one moment, mistake that for victory.
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: Bhratashree... not now. I beg you... not now.
speaker: ARJUNA

dialogue_text: Leave me, Arjuna! Let me go!
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: My brave Aryaputron... today I stand before all of you, stripped of everything but my faith... and not one of you can even look me in the eye.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Now let us see, Draupadi... who in this Sabha will come to save you.
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: Krishna...
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Govinda...
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Madhava...
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: You are my friend, my only refuge left. Today... I have no one else in this world.If my faith in you has ever been true... if Dharma still lives, anywhere, in this universe... then protect me now.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: What... what is happening?
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: No! This is impossible! It cannot be!
speaker: DUSHASANA

dialogue_text: Draupadi... you called. And I came.
speaker: KRISHNA

dialogue_text: I called everyone in this Sabha before I called you, Krishna. Everyone failed me.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Yes... And now, at last, you have placed your faith where no human hand, no human weakness, can ever fail you.
speaker: KRISHNA

dialogue_text: A thread was tied around my hand once, in another time, by a woman who did not stop to think of herself. I promised, that day, to return this debt a hundredfold. Today... I only keep my word.
speaker: KRISHNA

dialogue_text: When you had the strength to fight, you fought with everything you had. When everyone else failed you, you surrendered, not in defeat, but in faith, to me.
speaker: KRISHNA

dialogue_text: Dharma protects those who protect Dharma.
speaker: KRISHNA

dialogue_text: But remember this day for what it truly is. Not because Draupadi was humiliated... but because those who could have stopped it chose, instead, to remain silent.
speaker: KRISHNA

dialogue_text: An injustice does not become Dharma simply because it happens inside a royal court. And silence, however dignified it may look, does not make a wrong right.
speaker: KRISHNA

dialogue_text: Dharma is not passive obedience when Adharma has crossed every boundary set before it. When Adharma is allowed to grow unchecked, a day always comes when it must be stopped — by force, if nothing else will do.
speaker: KRISHNA

dialogue_text: Duryodhana! You have crossed every limit a man may cross today. Hear my vow — before this entire Sabha, before Krishna himself as my witness — with this very mace, I shall one day shatter the thigh you dared to bare before Draupadi. I will not rest; I will not sleep in peace, until that thigh lies broken in the dust.
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: Big words, Bhima.
speaker: DURYODHANA

dialogue_text: Remember them, Duryodhana. Every single word.
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: And hear my vow too, elders of this Sabha, since none of you found the courage to stop what was done to me today.This hair, which Dushasana's hands defiled before all of you — I shall never bind it again. Not for one single day. Not until I wash it, with my own two hands, in Dushasana's blood.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Dushasana! Hear me now, and hear me well. I swear before Agni, before this Sabha, before every god who is watching — I shall tear open your chest with these bare hands, and I shall drink the blood that flows from it. And with that very blood, Dushasana, I myself shall help Draupadi bind her hair once more, and see her vow fulfilled to the last drop.
speaker: BHIMA

dialogue_text: Enough! Enough — let this madness end here!
speaker: DHRITARASHTRA

dialogue_text: Dear putri Draupadi... today, this Sabha has brought a shame upon the Kuru name that no victory can ever wash away. I offer you a boon. Ask, and it shall be granted.
speaker: DHRITARASHTRA

dialogue_text: My first wish, Maharaj — let Yudhishthira be free. Let him never again, for the rest of his life, be called a slave.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Granted. Ask for another boon.
speaker: DHRITARASHTRA

dialogue_text: Free Bhima. Free Arjuna. Free Nakula. Free Sahadeva. And return to them the weapons that were taken from their hands.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Granted. All five Pandavas walk free from this hall today. Your wealth... your kingdom... everything that was lost is restored to you in full.
speaker: DHRITARASHTRA

dialogue_text: Ask for a third boon, Putri. Do not hesitate.
speaker: DHRITARASHTRA

dialogue_text: No, Maharaj. Two boons are enough for a woman who asked for nothing but her dignity. I will ask for nothing more.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: Draupadi... I failed you today, in every way a husband can fail his wife.
speaker: YUDHISHTHIRA

dialogue_text: Then let this day teach every soul in this hall what Dharma truly asks of us — before it is too late to learn it.
speaker: DRAUPADI

dialogue_text: The Pandavas were free.Their kingdom was returned.Draupadi had preserved their dignity.But Duryodhana could not accept defeat.Shakuni rolled the dice once again.This time, the stake was different.Twelve years in the forest... and one year in disguise.The Pandavas were summoned back.Yudhishthira played once more.And Shakuni won.The Pandavas left their kingdom...and began their thirteen-year exile.But the road they were about to walk...would lead them... to Kurukshetra — where every vow made in this hall would, at last, be kept.
speaker: VOICE OF TIME
